claims.text: The baseline material is an as-synthesized dendritic PtCuCo-based high-entropy-alloy nanocrystal catalyst.
The baseline PtCuCo-based nanocrystals have a uniform elemental distribution and a well-defined lattice structure.
Controlled thermal annealing will generate moderate tensile lattice strain in the PtCuCo-based nanocrystals.
A suitable annealing treatment can induce strain while preserving the dendritic morphology.
Tensile lattice distortion shifts or downshifts the d-band center of the catalyst's surface atoms.
A d-band-center shift tunes the adsorption and desorption energies of catalytic reactants and intermediates.
The proposed electronic shift weakens adsorption of poisoning species.
The proposed d-band shift preserves efficient ethanol activation despite weakening poisoning-species adsorption.
Balancing ethanol activation against poisoning-species adsorption enhances ethanol-oxidation activity.
The strain-induced adsorption balance increases selectivity for complete 12-electron ethanol oxidation.
The strain-induced adsorption balance improves long-term catalyst durability.
An optimal induced tensile strain will shift the ethanol-oxidation onset potential and enhance current density relative to the unannealed catalyst.
Annealing-induced changes in lattice parameter and d-band-center position will be measurable by XRD and XPS, respectively.
High-resolution TEM will show that the annealed catalyst retains the baseline morphology.
Excessive strain may degrade performance and cause sintering.
The mechanism applies under alkaline ethanol-oxidation conditions at fuel-cell-relevant temperatures.
The experiment will compare annealed and unannealed catalysts under otherwise identical ethanol-oxidation conditions.
Absence of measurable strain and d-band shifts despite altered catalytic performance is proposed as evidence against strain being responsible for the performance change.
